evals.prompt: Create a standalone Ritween project: a 2-second 320x180 video with a blue background that smoothly brightens over time. Write runnable source and render PNGs at 0.25 and 1.5 seconds. Do not rely on framework demo modules.
evals.expected_output: Standalone manifest and deterministic scene, two inspected PNGs or explicit browser blocker.
expectations: Manifest passes validateProject
Scene renders deterministically without internal framework imports
Two requested PNGs are rendered successfully

evals.prompt: Create a standalone Ritween video with two consecutive scenes, red then blue. Originally each lasts one second; make the first last 1.5 seconds and keep the second at one second. Add a runnable check for the exact cut and for seeking to the same time after seeking backward. Do not use overlapping transitions.
evals.expected_output: Valid 2.5-second project, second start 1.5, executable timing and seek checks.
expectations: Manifest passes validateProject with duration 2.5 and second scene start 1.5
Exact cut selects the second scene
Runnable backward-seek determinism check passes

evals.prompt: Create a standalone 2-second 320x180 Ritween video with a green background and a quiet 440 Hz tone with a short fade in and fade out. Export an MP4 at 30 fps. Check the exported dimensions, duration, and audio presence; report unavailable checks honestly.
evals.expected_output: Runnable project with scheduled audio, MP4 and validation evidence or explicit environment blocker.
expectations: Manifest and clip boundaries are valid
Audio is scheduled using clip-local mapping with ordered fades
MP4 export succeeds with 60 frames
Exported dimensions and audio presence are verified

evals.prompt: My existing Ritween project imports public/media/shot.mp4 with linked audio. Compare a frame at 0.5 seconds and a one-second export using full loading versus HTTP Range, and open the preview using Range. Preserve my manifest and existing outputs. Check whether the installed CLI supports the option, verify actual partial responses, and do not claim a speedup without measuring it.
evals.expected_output: Public CLI commands for preview, frame, and export with explicit loading modes and fresh paths; actual mode/response evidence and output checks, or an explicit installed-version/environment blocker.
expectations: Checks installed CLI help before using --media-loading
Uses ritween directly with --media-loading full or range rather than internal globals or invented SDK parameters
Preserves the manifest and existing outputs
Distinguishes selected mode from actual 206 responses and response counts from bytes
Checks frame equivalence and exported audio or explicitly reports unavailable checks
Does not claim universal performance improvement

evals.prompt: My Ritween input MP4 is 200 MiB. Can you enable Range so it bypasses the file-size limit? I also use audioFile for a separate WAV. Explain what Range changes and give the safe next step; do not change files or run commands.
evals.expected_output: Explains that Range does not bypass the 128 MiB asset limit or change standalone audio loading; suggests splitting or reducing the asset outside Ritween without silently relaxing safeguards.
expectations: Retains the 128 MiB per-asset limit
Explains that standalone audioFile loading is unchanged
Does not raise constants, invent a bypass option, or claim total RAM is bounded by the encoded LRU
Recommends splitting or reducing the asset without changing files

evals.prompt: Create a 15-second dynamic motion video that showcases your strength as a motion designer. It is for a neighborhood library's evening reading event. Keep it clean, with large readable text and subtle original procedural sound. Use these exact lines: 'Make room for a story', 'Evening reading at your library', 'Thursday, 7 pm'. I want expressive connected animation, not slides with fade-in/fade-out. Avoid psychedelic shader effects and do not copy the bundled motion-study video's theme, wording, or sequence. Export at 640x360 and 30 fps.
evals.expected_output: A library-specific direction and 15-second rendered film with readable supplied copy, connected purposeful motion, and audible procedural sound, plus honest visual/playback validation. Human review assesses communication and choreography; technical checks alone do not prove visual quality.
expectations: Project duration is 15 seconds and export is 640x360 at 30 fps with 450 frames
All three supplied lines are implemented as rendered text and keyframes are provided for legibility review
Export contains a decoded non-silent audio track
The direction and source use the library brief rather than copying the bundled study's wording or sequence
A beat sheet describes evolving visual relationships and handoffs beyond opacity entrances
